prerequisites: The TFG must be defended and evaluated once it is confirmed that the student has passed all other subjects of the study plan and therefore has all the necessary credits to obtain the Degree, except those corresponding to the TFG itself.

learning_outcomes.text: Integration capacity of all general and specific competencies within the scope of the Degree studies completed.
learning_outcomes.code: TFG (EFG1 in the Degree in Computer Engineering in Information Technologies)

learning_outcomes.text: The specific learning outcomes of the end-of-degree project will vary depending on the assigned topic by the tutor but, as a general rule, will be directly related to the specific objectives of the degree.

These results will be reflected in the individual completion, presentation, and defense before a university tribunal of an original project in the field of Engineering of a professional nature, in which all acquired competencies are synthesized and integrated.

syllabus_topics: Work topics within the area of Engineering in which the studies were pursued, as indicated in the objectives of each degree.
teaching_methods: Tutoring sessions with the TFG tutor

assessment_methods.method: Monitoring of the student's in-person activities by their academic tutor
Final document presented by the student
Public presentation of the work before the tribunal and subsequent debate with it

assessment_rules: The final definition of the evaluation system for the End-of-Degree Project will comply with the regulations defined in the End-of-Degree Project Regulations of the School of Engineering. Both ordinary and extraordinary evaluations are carried out through a public presentation before a tribunal of three professors from the School. Although the End-of-Degree Project may be part of a joint work, the presentation must be individual, clearly indicating the particular aspects or contribution of each student to the whole.
